changes.after: A monic cubic with dyadic coefficients
changes.reason: The denominator argument requires leading coefficient1; e.g.7 z^3-1 is a nonmonic dyadic counterexample to the broader wording. All support-vanishing polynomials used by the proof are monic, so formulas/controls are unchanged.

changes.before: Compactness of the feasible simplex after strict positivity stated
changes.after: First minimize on the closed nonnegative simplex, then prove positivity.
changes.reason: The strict-positive feasible subset is open; existence argument must begin with its compact closure.

changes.before: A zero facet puts the target on the boundary
changes.after: All facet slacks nonnegative and at least one zero imply feasible boundary membership.
changes.reason: A single zero slack does not imply membership if another slack is negative; actual code and exact checks already use all facet signs.

changes.before: P24 lower and upper gaps are 1/30 and 2/15
changes.after: Minimum lower P24 gap is 1/30 and the upper gap is 2/15.
changes.reason: The support has three lower facets; 1/30 names their minimum, not every lower slack.

changes.target: Mathematical duplicate grouping versus concrete API
changes.before: General moment geometry describes grouping duplicate squared nodes without restating API input restrictions.
changes.after: Concrete S11 input directions are strictly sorted and distinct; duplicate stored directions are rejected.
changes.reason: The mathematical grouping result is more general than the isolated API and does not authorize rewriting a caller's support.
